description:
**Divergence**:
- crate-jmap-mail-types/AGENTS.md L83-L91 — Design Constraints table has 6 rows
- crate-jmap-chat-types/AGENTS.md L130-L140 — Design Constraints table has 8 rows: adds `Constructors` (cites bd:JMAP-ly0n.7) and `Attribute order`

Both extra rows describe workspace-wide patterns that apply to ALL extension-types crates, not just chat-types. The Constructors row documents the workspace policy reversal recorded in bd:JMAP-sgrr.27 (the earlier 'no `::new()` methods' rule was effectively retired in favor of 'deserialize-from-JSON is the canonical path').

**Cookie-cutter / canonical-template inversion**: the workspace's canonical-templates rule (workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates" section) says contributors mirror the canonical's shape, and that changes to non-canonical siblings that diverge from the canonical must be cascaded canonical-first. Today chat-types describes the policy more fully than the canonical (mail-types) does. A contributor working on calendars-types, tasks-types, contacts-types, etc. would not see either policy unless they happened to read chat-types' AGENTS.md instead of mail-types'.

**Caller-observable cost**: directly — the Constructors policy applies to whether new code in (e.g.) calendars-types should ship a `pub fn new`. The canonical-template propagation is meaningless against a sibling whose AGENTS.md does not record the workspace-wide policy.

**Cross-reference**: bd:JMAP-sgrr.27 (the workspace policy decision); bd:JMAP-ops7.34 (the jscalendar-types constructor outlier that depends on this policy being in the canonical template).

**Fix**: lift the `Constructors` and `Attribute order` rows from chat-types' Design Constraints table into mail-types'. Word-for-word port is fine; the rows are workspace-policy citations, not chat-specific.
title: chat-types AGENTS.md Design Constraints table includes 'Constructors' and 'Attribute order' rows describing workspace-wide policy; canonical mail-types is silent on both — inverts canonical-template propagation direction
